structure.heading: Enterprise Bench Strength Assessment for Critical Roles (FY2026 Readiness)
text_content: **Enterprise Bench Strength Assessment for Critical Roles (FY2026 Readiness)**

As of 2026-05-01, 7 roles are designated as enterprise-critical: CEO, CFO, COO, CIO, CHRO, SVP Sales, and SVP Operations. Only 3 of the 7 enterprise-critical roles have at least one successor assessed as "Ready Now" as of 2026-05-01, representing roughly 43% of the critical-role population with immediate depth. The remaining four roles therefore lack an immediate internal replacement and heighten the enterprise’s exposure to unplanned leadership departures. This baseline informs targeted year-end readiness actions. Priorities are set for development and external sourcing.

Functional distribution as of 2026-05-01 shows uneven readiness across the enterprise. Finance and technology functions represent approximately 57% of current 'Ready' successor capacity, while sales and operations represent the remaining 43%. This skew creates concentration risk; loss in a high-readiness area still generates downstream gaps, and shortfalls in customer-facing or operational roles could materially impact revenue and delivery. Development priorities include cross-functional rotations, regulatory experience acquisition, and role-specific stretch assignments for identified successors. External benchmarking will validate candidate readiness and reviews.

The succession health target is 2 identified successors per critical role by 2026-12-31. Assuming a conservative baseline with one confirmed 'Ready Now' successor for each of the three roles, the enterprise must identify 11 additional successors to reach the 14-successor objective, averaging approximately 1.4 identified successors per month between 2026-05-01 and 2026-12-31. Priority actions: 1) CHRO-led talent reviews every six weeks; 2) targeted external hiring with time-to-fill under 90 days; 3) accelerated development assignments with measurable milestones. Accountability tracked monthly.

operations, single-event attrition could impair service delivery and financial stewardship within 30–60 days. Governance steps include monthly executive reviews by the CEO and CHRO, inclusion of succession metrics in quarterly risk reports beginning Q3 2026, and a defined escalation protocol for any unplanned vacancy in the enterprise-critical cohort. CHRO reports monthly to Board.

structure.heading: High-Potential Slate, Development Plans, and Emergency Succession Gaps (Next 12 Months)
text_content: **High-Potential Slate, Development Plans, and Emergency Succession Gaps (Next 12 Months)**

The high-potential slate includes exactly 6 candidates: Maya Patel, Jordan Kim, Elena Garcia, Priya Nair, Marcus Reed, and Chen Wei. Selected for cross-functional leadership potential and succession relevance across Finance, Technology, Operations, HR, Sales, and Product, the slate balances tenure and diversity. Short biographies and role maps are in the talent repository; stakeholder communication begins 2026-05-15.

Each high-potential candidate must complete an Individual Development Plan (IDP) with at least 3 actions by 2026-09-30. IDPs must list measurable milestones, mentorship, and stretch assignments. Progress will be tracked at quarterly checkpoints (next dates: 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30) and assessed for competency gains, documented feedback, and inclusion in the FY2026 readiness review, with a 100% completion target.

Emergency succession gaps are flagged for CFO and CIO with no "Ready Now" successor as of 2026-05-01. Immediate mitigation includes 90-day contingency plans: interim executive designation, accelerated development for high-potential candidates, and initiation of external search if internal readiness is insufficient. The CEO and Board have been notified; monthly progress reports will continue until closure or appointment.
